segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: So, I understand you’re interested in restaurant work?

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes. I’ve got a bit of experience and I can provide references.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: That’s good. I can check all that later. Now, Milo’s Restaurants have some vacancies at the moment. They’re a really good company to work for. Lots of benefits.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh right.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes. They’ve got a very good reputation for looking after staff. For example, all employees get training – even temporary staff.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh really? That’s quite unusual, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Certainly is.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: And do staff get free uniforms too?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Um ... you just need to wear a white T-shirt and black trousers, it says here. So I guess not ... But another benefit of working for a big company like this is that you can get a discount at any of their restaurants.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Even at weekends?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: No, but you’ll be working then anyway.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh yes. I suppose so. Most of their restaurants are in the city centre, aren’t they? So, easy to get to by bus?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes. That’s right. But if you have to do a late shift and finish work after midnight, the company will pay for you to get a taxi home.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I probably won’t need one. I think I’d use my bike.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK. Now, they do have some quite specific requirements for the kind of person they’re looking for. Milo’s is a young, dynamic company and they’re really keen on creating a strong team. It’s really important that you can fit in and get on well with everyone.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yeah. I’ve got no problem with that. It sounds good, actually. The last place I worked for was quite demanding too. We had to make sure we gave a really high level of service.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: That’s good to hear because that will be equally important at Milo’s. I know they want people who have an eye for detail.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That’s fine. I’m very used to working in that kind of environment.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Perfect. So the only other thing that’s required is good communication skills, so you’ll need to have a certificate in English.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Sure. ——

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: OK. Let’s have a look at the current job vacancies at Milo’s. The first one is in Wivenhoe Street.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Sorry, where?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Wivenhoe. W-l-V-E-N-H-O-E. It’s quite central, just off Cork Street.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Oh right.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: They’re looking for a breakfast supervisor.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That would be OK.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: So you’re probably familiar with the kind of responsibilities involved. Obviously checking that all the portions are correct, etc., and then things like checking all the procedures for cleaning the equipment are being followed.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: OK. And what about the salary? In my last job I was getting £9.50 per hour. I was hoping to get a bit more than that.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Well, to begin with, you’d be getting £9.75 but that goes up to £11.25 after three months.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: That’s not too bad. And I suppose it’s a very early start?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Mmm. That’s the only unattractive thing about this job. But then you have the afternoons and evenings free. So the restaurant starts serving breakfast from 7 a.m. And you’d have to be there at 5.30 to set everything up. But you’d be finished at 12.30.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Mmm. Well, as you say, there are advantages to that.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Now, you might also be interested in the job at the City Road branch. That’s for a junior chef, so again a position of responsibility.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I might prefer that, actually.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Right, well obviously this role would involve supporting the sous chef and other senior staff. And you’d be responsible for making sure there’s enough stock each week – and sorting out all the deliveries.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: I’ve never done that before, but I imagine it’s fairly straightforward, once you get the hang of it.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: Yes, and you’d be working alongside more experienced staff to begin with, so I’m sure it wouldn’t be a problem. The salary’s slightly higher here. It’s an annual salary of £23,000.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: I know that if they like you, it’s likely you’ll be promoted quite quickly. So that’s worth thinking about.

segments.speaker: MAN
segments.en: Yes. It does sound interesting. What are the hours like?

segments.speaker: WOMAN
segments.en: The usual, I think. There’s a lot of evening and weekend work, but they’re closed on Mondays. But you do get one Sunday off every four weeks. So would you like me to send off your ...

Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
